# Brightness & contrast

The everyday image adjustments: brightness, contrast, saturation and vibrance, applied to display-encoded values so the sliders behave like a photo editor’s.

<EffectDemo effect="brightness-contrast" />

## Usage

```ts
import { EffectComposer } from '@mk7s/xtree/core';
import { brightnessContrast } from '@mk7s/xtree/effects/brightness-contrast';

const composer = new EffectComposer(renderer);
composer.setScene(scene, camera);
composer.add(brightnessContrast({ preset: 'punchy' }));
renderer.setAnimationLoop(() => composer.render());
```

Every parameter is also a property: `effect.brightness = 0`. Uniform changes take effect on the next frame without recompiling.

## Parameters

| Parameter    | Type   | Default | Range  | Description                                                                              |
| ------------ | ------ | ------- | ------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `brightness` | number | `0`     | -1 – 1 | Added to every channel.                                                                  |
| `contrast`   | number | `0`     | -1 – 1 | Spreads values away from mid-grey (positive) or flattens them (negative).                |
| `saturation` | number | `0`     | -1 – 1 | Color intensity; −1 is greyscale.                                                        |
| `vibrance`   | number | `0`     | -1 – 1 | Saturation that favors muted colors, leaving saturated ones and skin tones mostly alone. |

Every effect also has `blend` (any of the 26 [blend modes](/reference/shaders#modes)), `opacity` (0–1) and `enabled`.

## Presets

| Preset   | Settings                                                 |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `punchy` | `contrast: 0.25`, `saturation: 0.15`, `vibrance: 0.35`   |
| `faded`  | `brightness: 0.05`, `contrast: -0.3`, `saturation: -0.3` |
| `muted`  | `saturation: -0.55`, `vibrance: -0.2`                    |
| `bright` | `brightness: 0.08`, `contrast: 0.1`                      |

Apply one with `brightnessContrast({ preset: 'name' })` or `effect.applyPreset('name')`; presets start from the defaults.

## Details

- **Family:** Color & tone · tracked as story X3.1 in the [plan](https://github.com/s4njee/xtree/blob/main/plan.md).
- **Passes:** reads only its own pixel, so it merges into the pass before it.
- **Masks:** set `effect.mask` to a texture, depth range or selection to limit where it applies; see [masks](/guide/masks).
- **Motion:** Static: nothing animates.
- **Cost:** 0.0 ms added to a 960×540 frame on CI container (SwiftShader software renderer) (2026-10-11). A software renderer: use it to compare effects, not to predict GPU times.
- **Size:** 7.1 KB gzip budget for `@mk7s/xtree/effects/brightness-contrast`, including the shared effect runtime.

## Credits

Original implementation (MIT). References: Standard brightness, contrast and saturation adjustments on display-encoded values; Vibrance as saturation weighted by inverse chroma.

## Related

- [Hue / saturation](./hue-saturation) — Rotates hues, scales saturation and lifts or lowers lightness in OKLCH, a perceptual space, so a hue shift does not make yellows glow or blues go dark.
- [Exposure & gamma](./exposure-gamma) — Exposure in photographic stops, a black-level offset and a gamma curve, applied in linear light before tone mapping, like adjusting a camera rather than a screenshot.
- [LUT color grading](./lut) — Grades the image through a 3D lookup table, such as a `.cube` file exported from Resolve, Premiere or Photoshop, with tetrahedral interpolation.
